scope: Stage 80 only, on the same OpenRouter account with ZDR enabled. Exercise the original native Codex request bodies, then the policy-shaped HTTP fixtures and native metadata run. Report results before product implementation.

key_setup.condition: Use a dedicated key on the stage 60 account with at least USD 3.00 available and a non-resetting limit at or below USD 5.00 including BYOK. If none is supplied, approval includes one management POST to create the specified key before the run.

controls: Verify the stage 70 pass, its stage 60 ZDR prerequisite, the earlier stage 80 HTTP 402, the native Codex binary and all fixture hashes locally before dispatch. Use the metadata decision from the verified cost receipt.

The 402 reported 49,962 affordable tokens with USD 1.99848 available. At that observed ratio, the 65,536-token allowance corresponds to approximately USD 2.62 for one request. The proposed USD 5.00 ceiling leaves headroom for input and successive turns. Actual cost and provider admission can vary.

Verify the dedicated key once by GET /api/v1/key before any generation. Keep account ZDR enabled. Preserve both native baselines by value, including the absence of max_output_tokens. The policy replays and the additional native metadata run require provider.zdr=true.

Run stage 80 once under a fresh ledger for the approved digest. Reserve each request before sending, including client retries, tool continuations and auxiliary creates. Stop after an inconclusive result, budget exhaustion or the 15-minute deadline. All redirects stay unfollowed.
codex: Run native Codex exec and exec resume on both slugs with the client's default tool declarations and no policy mutation. A fresh isolated home, workspace, thread and loopback credential belong to each run. Only the test bridge holds the OpenRouter key. Account ZDR applies to both unmodified native baselines. The bridge rejects store=true. All 13 pinned Responses fixtures have store=false.

The scratch project has a single input file, fixture.txt, containing FORGE_FIXTURE_173. The first prompt requests exactly 'cat fixture.txt'. The resumed prompt asks the client to write the word from turn one to proof.txt with 'echo WORD > proof.txt'. Verify the resulting file. These are the only local commands the bridge accepts.

Replay each checksum-pinned synthetic fixture with provider.zdr=true. For each tool request, append the freshly returned output items, including any opaque reasoning and matching call ID, followed by the synthetic read result. Record whether encrypted replay was exercised. Title fixtures require a strict JSON object with a 1–36 character title and no additional fields.

The stage 70 stream with routing metadata identified Azure. Enable X-OpenRouter-Metadata on the 13 policy replays and on the additional native Astra read/edit run with provider.zdr=true and web search disabled.

Native calls may send bundled client instructions, tool schemas, scratch paths and newly generated client IDs. Synthetic HTTP fixtures replace local paths, client-generated IDs and prose. Native default-tool declarations can include web search on Gemini. The task requires only the two local scratch commands.

The 10 tool fixtures use two creates each and the three title fixtures use one each. At the observed loopback rate, the three native read/edit runs use four creates apiece, leaving five of the 40 generation attempts for additional Codex traffic. Both models map to themselves under the bundled ZDR policy.
